title: The 10 Best Laser Levels
subtitle: Self-leveling cross-line and 360-degree laser levels for hanging pictures, cabinets, tile and ceilings, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A self-leveling laser projects a level (and plumb) line across a wall or a whole room, so you can hang a row of cabinets or tile a backsplash without a 4-foot level and a pencil. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (a green beam, full 360-degree lines, a rechargeable battery, a pulse mode for outdoor detectors and a tripod in the box). Cross-line lasers cover one wall at a time; 3x360 lasers wrap the whole room. They run from about $35 to $499 for DEWALT's 3x360 green kit.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

avoid.name: AikTryee Laser Level Line Tool, Cross Line Laser Leveler Beam Tool with 8ft Tape
avoid.flag: Not self-leveling; you level it by eye
avoid.verdict: A $10 laser pointer with bubble vials, sold as a laser level. For $25 more, the Lusweimi actually levels itself and lists its accuracy.
reasons: It isn't self-leveling. You line up a bubble vial by eye while it's stuck to the wall, so the line is only as level as your read of the bubble, which is exactly the error a laser level is supposed to remove.
The listing gives no accuracy figure at all, even though it's sold for cabinets and tile, the jobs where 1/8 inch matters.
It projects the line from where it's mounted on the wall, so it can't throw a level line across a room or onto an opposite wall like the self-leveling lasers above.

buyers_guide.a: A cross-line laser projects one horizontal and one vertical line on the wall in front of it, which covers pictures, shelves and a run of cabinets. A 3x360 laser wraps level and plumb lines around the whole room, which helps with ceilings, wall-to-wall tile and framing.
Green beams look about 2 to 4 times brighter to the eye, so they're easier to see in lit rooms and at distance. Red lasers cost less and run longer on batteries.
A pendulum inside swings the laser level by itself within about 3-4 degrees. If you set it on an uneven surface beyond that, it blinks to warn you. Lock the pendulum before moving it.
Outdoors or in bright sun you often can't see the beam. Pulse mode makes the laser flash at a rate a laser detector (sold separately) can pick up, extending the range to 150 feet or more.

buyers_guide.q: How accurate does a laser level need to be?
buyers_guide.a: About 1/8 inch at 30 feet is the common standard and fine for cabinets and tile. Many budget lasers don't publish an accuracy figure at all; check one against a known level line before relying on it.
